DigitalOcean Holdings (NYSE:DOCN) presented its second quarter 2026 earnings results on August 4, 2026, showcasing a dramatic acceleration in growth driven by its AI-native cloud platform.
The company reported revenue growth of 29% year-over-year, more than double the 14% growth rate from the same quarter a year earlier, as AI-focused customers increasingly adopted its integrated infrastructure and inference services.
Despite beating Wall Street expectations with adjusted earnings of $0.45 per share on revenue of $281.2 million, shares initially fell 7.85% in premarket trading before recovering.
The stock has since rebounded to $131.50, up 3.4% from the previous close of $127.17, reflecting investor reassessment of the company’s long-term growth trajectory after a 371% gain over the past year.
...
AI Customer ARR reached $234 million, growing 212% year-over-year.
The composition of this growth is particularly noteworthy: inference services grew 762% year-over-year, while core cloud services for AI customers expanded 158%.
The shift away from bare metal infrastructure is evident, with non-bare-metal services now representing 85% of AI Customer ARR, up from just 43% in Q2 2025.
...
For the third quarter, the company expects revenue of $304-$307 million, representing 32-34% year-over-year growth.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance increased to $1.17-$1.18 billion from the prior range of $1.13-$1.15 billion, representing a $37.5 million increase at the midpoint.
This implies full-year growth of 30-31%, up from the previous expectation of 25-27%.
The company also raised its adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 38.5-39.5% and increased non-GAAP diluted earnings per share expectations to $1.35-$1.40 from $1.10-$1.20.
...

{"figures":[{"fact_key":"Start date","value":"2025-09-10"},{"fact_key":"End date","value":"2026-09-09"},{"fact_key":"Total return on contributions","value":188.87},{"fact_key":"Benchmark return","value":12.07},{"fact_key":"Return difference versus benchmark","value":176.8},{"fact_key":"Worst drop from a prior high","value":-42.12},{"fact_key":"Total money contributed","value":2300.0},{"fact_key":"Ending portfolio value","value":6644.07},{"fact_key":"Highest portfolio value","value":8648.6},{"fact_key":"Contribution schedule","value":"monthly"},{"fact_key":"Executed fills","value":13}],"language":"en","text":"From September 10, 2025 to September 9, 2026, DOCN went from being a relatively ordinary cloud-computing story to a major AI-growth story in the market’s eyes. The business results improved steadily: DigitalOcean reported third-quarter 2025 revenue up 16% year over year and raised its full-year outlook. In February, it reported fourth-quarter revenue of $242 million, up 18%, while saying that larger customers and AI demand were accelerating. Its first-quarter 2026 report showed revenue up 22%, AI customer annual recurring revenue up 221%, and the launch of a broader AI-native cloud platform. By August, second-quarter revenue growth had accelerated to 29%, and the company raised its 2026 outlook again. These company-reported results are evidence of improving growth and stronger AI demand, not proof that every share-price move was caused by one announcement.

The stock’s rise appears to have reflected investors placing a much higher value on that AI opportunity. The inference is supported by the sequence of faster growth, sharply higher AI-related customer revenue, and repeated increases to management’s outlook. The market also had reasons to hesitate. DigitalOcean disclosed an 11.9 million-share follow-on offering in its first-quarter results, which can concern investors because issuing more shares can reduce each existing shareholder’s slice of the company. The stock therefore did not behave like a smooth climb. It suffered a 42.12% drop from a previous high during the test, meaning that holding through the period included a very painful temporary loss before the later recovery.

For the monthly-contribution test, that rough ride mattered. The strategy made 13 purchases rather than putting all the money in at once, so some later contributions bought shares after declines. That can make a recovery more helpful, but it does not remove the emotional difficulty of watching a holding fall sharply. The portfolio ultimately ended at $6644.07 after $2300.0 had been contributed, although its highest recorded value was $8648.6. In other words, the test finished well above the amount paid in, but below its peak, so the experience was profitable and still unsettled at the end.

Against SPY, the result was unusually strong. DOCN produced a 188.87% return on contributions, while the benchmark returned 12.07%. That is a 176.8 percentage-point advantage for the test. The comparison says that this particular concentrated bet benefited enormously from DOCN’s re-rating around AI and accelerating growth during this window. It does not show that DOCN was safer: the large drawdown and the fact that one company drove the result show the opposite. SPY offered exposure to a much broader group of companies, so its more modest result came with a much less company-specific story."}
